title: Workers start through a launcher command the operator sets, and kbmon reads agent states from an external source through a JSON contract
goal: backlog.json takes a launcher (an argv template with the worker's directory and command) that dispatch uses in place of its own detached start, the current start staying the default; kbmon takes an agent-states command whose JSON lines give a pid or session id and a state (working, blocked, idle, done) and shows that state beside the presence lease; both contracts are documented with no product named, so a terminal workspace manager or any other runtime can host the workers and report their states; backlog.py config prints both settings.

run: import subprocess as s,sys;p=s.run([sys.executable,'_tools/backlog.py','config'],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=60,check=True);print(p.stdout);sys.exit(0 if 'launcher' in p.stdout and 'agent_states' in p.stdout else 1)
